SATOM 3.2.0

An HTTP Observatory grades every site your appliances publish and fixes it on the FortiWeb, the Transaction Tracer becomes a page with cookies and a HAR viewer, profiles can be confined to some ADOMs, and Studio gains a Script Library with database-fed forms.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user

Released: 2026-10-16 · All releases

In short#

SATOM 3.2 is about what your appliances publish. The new HTTP Observatory grades every site behind a FortiWeb server policy or a FortiADC virtual server with the MDN HTTP Observatory tests, says whether the FortiWeb, the application or the certificate caused each finding, and applies the FortiWeb fix with a preview of the grade it gives. The Transaction Tracer becomes a page with cookie analysis and a HAR viewer.

The release also lets an administrator confine a profile to some ADOMs, adds a Script Library to Studio, extends the Certificate Manager (CSRs for another CA, imports, staged rotation, a revocation register, an OPNsense CA signer), and closes a long list of findings from an internal security audit. Read Before you upgrade.

What's new#

HTTP Observatory#

Troubleshooting → HTTP Observatory lists every published site of an appliance and grades it with the MDN HTTP Observatory's twelve tests and scoring: the same grade the public scanner gives, except that the HSTS preload list is not consulted. Each result carries who produced it — FortiWeb, the application, the certificate, or nobody — and on a FortiWeb the fix: header rows, HSTS, the HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect and cookie flags. Preview changes lists the writes, the server policies they reach and the projected grade; Apply writes, re-reads each change from the device and grades the site again. Grades are kept per site, and a scheduled action grades on a schedule. See HTTP Observatory.

Transaction Tracer as a page#

The tracer left the header Tools menu for Troubleshooting → Transaction Tracer. Each leg shows the cookies it set with their flags and what a browser will do with them, and both legs together show the cookies the appliance issued, removed or rewrote. Reveal values (new permission monitoring.reveal_secrets, Administrator only) shows credential values without ever writing them to the audit log. The HAR viewer reads the trace's HAR or any HAR file, in the browser. A line under the legs gives the security-header grade of the response. See Transaction tracer.

Profiles confined to ADOMs#

A permission profile can be limited to some ADOMs. A confined user sees only those ADOMs; their Global view is the union of them, and database consoles that cannot be scoped are refused. While building it, several pages that loaded a record of another ADOM by its id were closed. See Users and profiles.

Script Library#

Studio → Script Library: Python scripts with a form, kept as small projects, tested and published by administrators and run by operators in a sandbox. Every edit is a version you can compare with any other; forms can take values from the SATOM database (one row, several rows or a whole result set); automations accept cron schedules. See Script Library.

Certificate Manager#

Generate a CSR for another CA and import what it signs; import certificates made elsewhere; rotate a certificate in stages; keep a revocation register; sign with a CA held in an OPNsense firewall. The Certificate Manager is in every ADOM. See Certificates.

WAF Artifacts#

Fetch from the application brings in the WSDL and XML Schema files a SOAP service publishes, following their imports. A policy clone or migration now creates the schemas a WSDL imports before the WSDL. The pages now state that a FortiWeb Entire backup carries these files encrypted and that restoring it does not bring them back. See WAF Artifacts.

Smaller additions#

  • Diagnostic Battery per ADOM, and Diagnose Log Collection in every device ADOM.
  • API tokens: every non-destructive action has a capability. See API tokens.
  • Every device can be named on a change request, FortiGate included.
  • Settings → General → System packages, and Libraries changes run as a job.

What changes for you#

  • The Transaction Tracer is no longer in the Tools menu: it is under Troubleshooting.
  • Administrators who used to see every ADOM keep seeing every ADOM: a profile is confined only when an administrator chooses ADOMs for it.
  • Integration hook secrets and the alert webhook secret follow the vault mode.

Fixed#

  • Published-service probes read custom services and a policy's HTTPS service (custom ports used to become 80 or 443).
  • A cookie the appliance rewrites is no longer called "identical" by the tracer.
  • A release that adds a table no longer takes the web service down at boot.
  • A psycopg upgrade from the Libraries card no longer takes both HA nodes down.
  • Pages opened from the menu work without a refresh; Copy on a CSR works.
  • Alert email: messages carry a Message-ID; delivered-but-unsigned is an error.

Security#

  • Integration hooks run in a jail with a filtered network.
  • Signed releases, node request signing and console hardening; the operator CLI no longer runs the application tree as root.
  • Fixes from the internal code audit: account and two-factor flows, ADOM and profile authorisation, stored cross-site scripting, transport between nodes. See Security model.

Before you upgrade#

  • This release is published as source on GitHub (tag v3.2.0). No new installers, container image or offline update package were built for it; the newest of those remain the 3.1.0 ones.
  • The database schema gains tables (observatory_scans and others); the upgrade migrates it.

Learn more#

  • Full list of changes: the CHANGELOG in the repository.
